abstract: Let $X$ be a projective K3 surface, $h$ an ample class with $h^2 = 2d$, and $H = h\boxtimes h$. A Hodge class $\beta$ on $X\times X$ has projection degrees $x_1, x_2$, an $\mathrm{NS}\otimes\mathrm{NS}$ part, and an eigenvalue $t_\beta$, its action on $H^{2,0}(X)$. Pseudoeffective classes satisfy $|t_\beta|^2\le x_1x_2$ (Lehmann–Ottem) and $\beta\cdot H\ge2d|t_\beta|$. (C) For rational $x_1, x_2$ and rational eigenvalue $u$, the first bound is the only constraint: the class $x_1P_1 + x_2P_2 + N + [u] + yH$ is pseudoeffective for some $y$ if and only if $x_1, x_2\ge0$ and $u^2\le x_1x_2$, and then it is the class of an effective $\mathbb Q$-cycle for all large rational $y$. The boundary is attained by graphs of pairs of multiplication maps on an elliptic family covering $X$, a construction of cm_symmetry_scout (rStation 145). So, after adding enough $H$ and away from the boundary $u^2 = x_1x_2$, a gap between strongly positive and pseudoeffective classes on K3 squares, as in rStation 148, needs an irrational eigenvalue; boundary gaps are not excluded. (D) An effective $\mathbb R$-cycle attains $\beta\cdot H = 2d|t_\beta|$ if and only if it is a nonnegative combination of fibres and graphs of $h$-preserving automorphisms with a common eigenvalue. Such a cycle is conformal for the Ricci-flat metric, and curvature forces it to be isometric. Consequently, on every projective K3 surface the diagonal is the unique effective $\mathbb R$-cycle in its class, which Lehmann and Ottem proved for very general $X$. For Picard number one and $d\ge2$, the class $2(P_1 + P_2 + H/(2d)) - \Delta$ meets both bounds with equality but is not effective, so it is either pseudoeffective only through cycles of unbounded degree or not pseudoeffective; we do not know which.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the minor changes requested in the version 1 report. No statement changes.
1. Abstract and introduction: the claim that a positivity gap "needs an irrational eigenvalue" is qualified. It now holds after adding enough H and away from the boundary u^2 = x1x2, as in Corollary 3.3, and the text says that rational-eigenvalue gaps on the boundary are not excluded (Question 5.3).
2. Section 4: a paragraph "Comparison with trianalytic rigidity" explains that in the equality case of Lemma 4.1 the graph plane is complex for every induced complex structure of a suitable product hyperkähler structure, and relates step (4) of Theorem D to Verbitsky's desingularisation theorem as recalled by Soldatenkov and Verbitsky (arXiv:1409.1100, Thm 1.2, new ref. [14]) and to rStation 80, Rem. 2.2 (new ref. [15]). The curvature proof is kept. For the local-isometry extension, the argument (injectivity radius, continuation by the exponential map, monodromy) is now recalled in the text, with Kobayashi–Nomizu Vol. I, Ch. VI, §6 as the reference.
3. Corollary 5.2: the cycle-level statement S = Σ a_i({p_i} × X) + Σ b_j(X × {q_j}) + cΔ, with fibres over several points allowed, is separated from its class aP1 + bP2 + c[Δ].
4. Inline mathematics in the manuscript and in the metadata abstract is now in LaTeX delimiters. "c is the ratio of the projection degrees" is corrected to "c^2 is the ratio".
5. After Lemma 2.1, a remark notes that the lemma also follows from Lieberman's theorem (new ref. [13]) as explained by Lehmann and Ottem, §2.2; the direct proof is kept because it gives the orthogonal decomposition.
title: Rational eigenvalues and the degree face of the pseudoeffective cone of a K3 square
